Internal helper: jfreq()'s footnote under a table with a blank row

Source: R/classify.R
dot-jst_blank_footnote.Rd

Three lines, one sentence each (voice Rule E): what the row is, with the two kinds counted apart when both occur; that it is counted as valid – "Valid %" reads to this audience as though blanks were excluded, and they are not; and the one way to change that. A legend printed with its table, on stdout, as jscreen()'s star legend is.

Usage

.jst_blank_footnote(counts, declare = TRUE, declare_arg = "codes = \"\"")

Arguments

counts

A .jst_blank_counts() list.

declare

Logical; FALSE for a factor, whose blank levels jdeclare_missing() cannot declare.

declare_arg

Character(1); the codes argument the declare route names (.jst_text_declare_args()), or NULL when no declaration can hold the blank beside the values declared.

Value

Character(1), newline-joined; "" when there is no blank.

Details

Since Slate E5 (ruling R27) the way out names both routes, a line each: jencode() gives the blank cells a code, jdeclare_missing() with codes = "" declares them missing. A factor gets the one jencode() line it had, since jdeclare_missing() refuses a factor.

Since Session 374 (the S373 item) the declare route names the values the variable already declares as well – codes = c("UNKNOWN", "") – since a declaration replaces a variable's values and codes = "" alone dropped them; past a text variable's three the jencode() line alone is given, as for a factor.
